analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a universal-primer Oxford Nanopore sequencing workflow for rapid and high-throughput genotyping of Influenza A viruses. The workflow uses conserved terminal region primers to amplify all genomic segments in a single process, enabling real-time monitoring and post-run clade assignment. A total of 95 respiratory samples collected between October and November 2025 that tested positive for Influenza A by qPCR were analyzed. Using predefined criteria for genome recovery, 71 samples met the metrics for near-complete genome recovery, while 20 samples had partial coverage. Four samples produced no mapped reads. Despite incomplete genome recovery in some cases, clade-level genotyping was achieved for 87 samples (91.6%). The study highlights the feasibility of this approach for scalable clinical-laboratory surveillance, supporting efficient molecular surveillance and public health decision-making. The workflow's effectiveness was demonstrated through real-time monitoring and clade assignment using Nextclade against reference A/Darwin/6/2021. The evidence is strong, with high confidence in the workflow's performance for Influenza A genotyping.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在标准化并评估一种针对流感A病毒基因型鉴定的通用引物牛津纳米孔测序工作流程,包括实时监测和运行后分支分配。

papers.title_zh: B-312 流感A病毒通用基因型鉴定:一种使用通用片段引物的敏捷牛津纳米孔测序工作流程
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Influenza A is a segmented negative-sense RNA virus with eight genomic segments. Efficient genome characterization is essential for molecular surveillance and public health decision-making. Universal primers targeting conserved terminal regions enable amplification of all segments within a single workflow, supporting rapid sequencing and genotype assignment. This study aimed to standardize and evaluate a universal-primer Oxford Nanopore workflow for Influenza A genotyping, including real-time monitoring and post-run clade assignment. Methods Residual eluates from respiratory samples collected between October and November 2025 that tested positive for Influenza A by qPCR were used for genomic surveillance. Samples were de-identified and submitted to cDNA synthesis (High-Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit) supplemented with universal primers targeting conserved terminal regions. Amplicon enrichment was performed with the same primer sets and Q5® High-Fidelity 2X Master Mix; products were assessed by agarose gel electrophoresis. Barcoding used a transposition-based approach, libraries were adapter-ligated, and sequencing was performed on MinION flowcells. Real-time monitoring was performed with RAMPART. Consensus generation was performed in EPI2ME, followed by clade/genotype analysis using Nextclade for Influenza A(H3N2) HA and NA against reference A/Darwin/6/2021. Results A library of 95 samples was sequenced for 5 hours and 31 minutes, generating 752,910 reads. Using predefined criteria for near-complete genome recovery (minimum 20× depth and =75% horizontal genome coverage), 71/95 samples met the established metrics. Four samples produced no mapped reads. The remaining 20 samples yielded partial genome recovery with mean horizontal coverage of 52% (range 8.08%–74.94%). Despite incomplete whole-genome recovery in a subset, clade-level genotyping was achieved for 87/95 samples (91.6%), indicating that sufficient subtype/clade-informative sequence was obtained for most specimens. Eight samples were not genotyped: four due to absence of mapped reads and four due to insufficient coverage to support confident assignment. Conclusion This universal-primer Nanopore workflow enabled rapid, high-throughput Influenza A genotyping with real-time monitoring and high clade-assignment success (91.6%) in a single MinION run. QC thresholds of 20× depth and =75% horizontal coverage effectively identified samples suitable for near-complete genome recovery, while clade assignment remained feasible for most samples despite heterogeneous input quality. This approach supports agile clinical-laboratory surveillance with scalable implementation.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 流感A病毒是一种具有八个基因组片段的分节负链RNA病毒。对分子特征进行高效鉴定对于公共卫生决策至关重要。针对保守末端区域的通用引物能够在单一工作流程中扩增所有片段,支持快速测序和基因型分配。本研究旨在标准化并评估一种针对流感A病毒基因型鉴定的通用引物牛津纳米孔测序工作流程,包括实时监测和运行后分支分配。方法 使用2025年10月至11月期间通过qPCR检测出流感A病毒的呼吸道样本残余洗脱液进行基因组监测。样本去标识化后,使用High-Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit进行cDNA合成,并补充针对保守末端区域的通用引物。使用相同的引物集合和Q5® High-Fidelity 2X Master Mix进行扩增子富集;产物通过琼脂糖凝胶电泳进行评估。条形码使用基于转座的策略,库通过接头连接,测序在MinION流细胞上进行。实时监测使用RAMPART进行。共识生成在EPI2ME中完成,随后使用Nextclade对流感甲型H3N2流感病毒的HA和NA进行分支/基因型分析,参考A/Darwin/6/2021。结果 对95个样本进行了5小时31分钟的测序,生成了752,910条读数。根据预定义的标准(最小20×深度和=75%水平基因组覆盖),71/95个样本符合已建立的指标。4个样本未产生任何映射读数。其余20个样本产生了部分基因组恢复,平均水平覆盖率为52%(范围8.08%–74.94%)。尽管部分样本未能实现完整的基因组恢复,仍有87/95个样本(91.6%)实现了分支水平的基因型鉴定,表明大多数样本获得了足够的亚型/分支信息序列。8个样本未进行基因型鉴定:其中4个因无映射读数,另外4个因覆盖不足而无法进行可靠分配。结论 这种通用引物的纳米孔测序工作流程能够在单次MinION运行中实现快速、高通量的流感A病毒基因型鉴定,同时具备实时监测和高分支分配成功率(91.6%)。20×深度和=75%水平覆盖的质控阈值有效识别了适合近完全基因组恢复的样本,尽管输入质量存在异质性,大多数样本仍能进行分支分配。这种方法支持临床实验室的敏捷监测,并具有可扩展的实施能力。

papers.title: ATTITUDES AND PRACTICES TOWARDS COVID-19 AND SEASONAL FLU VACCINES AND VACCINATION IN THE GENERAL POPULATION AND AMONG MEDICAL PROFESSIONALS
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has led to the development of several types of vaccines, among which messenger RNA (mRNA)-based vaccines have represented a significant breakthrough. This study aimed to evaluate attitudes towards COVID-19 and seasonal influenza vaccination among the general population and individuals with a medical background. A questionnaire was developed to collect sociodemographic data, personal health information, vaccination status, and information on participants’ attitudes towards and knowledge of vaccines. The profile of the typical participant was an employed woman with tertiary education, living with another person in an urban area and reporting generally good health. The typical participant had received at least two doses of the Sputnik V vaccine. Participants generally expressed favourable attitudes towards regular COVID-19 vaccination. The results showed no apparent differences between participants with and without a medical background regarding vaccine choice, the decision to receive a third dose, or seasonal influenza vaccination. Similarly, no apparent differences were observed in attitudes towards the AstraZeneca vaccine or mandatory COVID-19 vaccination between respondents with and without a medical background.

papers.title: Aircraft wastewater virome surveillance from domestic and international flights reveals viral diversity among travellers: A proof-of-concept study from Gujarat, India.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aircraft wastewater surveillance (AWS) at airports is an emerging method for detecting pathogens shed by international and domestic travellers. Global spread of infectious diseases occurs rapidly through air travel, and implementing surveillance systems at airports can help identify emerging viruses and track pathogens at scale. We aimed to characterize the viral diversity shed by travellers, which may represent routine viral circulation or active infection, at Ahmedabad airport in Gujarat. METHODS: We collected wastewater samples from domestic and international terminals where domestic flights connect to 18 states and 3 Union Territories, while international flights operate across 16 destinations in 11 countries. Samples were collected from June 2024 to November 2025. We used a capture probe-based enrichment approach for virome surveillance and detected multiple viruses of public health importance. RESULTS: We identified a total of 40 viral families and 315 viral species, with a median of 71 genomes/segments detected per sample in domestic wastewater and 48.5 genomes/segments per sample in international wastewater. We detected several respiratory and enteric viruses, including Influenza A virus, SARS-CoV-2, Human mastadenovirus A, Human mastadenovirus B, Noroviruses, Rotavirus A, Hepatitis A virus, Astrovirus MLB1, Human mastadenovirus F. Among these, certain viruses showed relatively higher mean RPKMF abundance in either domestic or international wastewater samples such as Bovine rotavirus A, Human rotavirus ID45/2, and BK polyomavirus observed in international wastewater samples, whereas Aichivirus A1, Norovirus GII.2, and Human immunodeficiency virus 1 showed higher abundance in domestic wastewater samples. We also detected multiple Influenza virus subtypes, including Influenza A subtypes H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, H7N1, and H9N2, along with Influenza B and Influenza C viruses. CONCLUSIONS: Continuous surveillance can provide early warning signals to public health authorities, timely decision-making and coordinated responses can reduce the spread of disease which also requires collaboration with national and international health authorities.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterize the viral diversity shed by travellers at Ahmedabad airport in Gujarat using aircraft wastewater surveillance. Wastewater samples were collected from domestic and international terminals between June 2024 and November 2025. The methods involved a capture probe-based enrichment approach to detect multiple viruses of public health importance. The main results showed the identification of 40 viral families and 315 viral species, with a median of 71 genomes/segments detected per sample in domestic wastewater and 48.5 genomes/segments per sample in international wastewater. The study detected several respiratory and enteric viruses, including Influenza A virus, SARS-CoV-2, and others. It also identified multiple Influenza virus subtypes, such as H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, H7N1, and H9N2, along with Influenza B and Influenza C viruses. The authors concluded that continuous surveillance can provide early warning signals to public health authorities, enabling timely decision-making and coordinated responses to reduce disease spread. The findings suggest that wastewater surveillance at airports can be a valuable tool for monitoring viral diversity and detecting emerging pathogens, which may inform public health strategies for disease prevention and control. The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength for the study.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 飞机废水监测(AWS)在机场是一种新兴的检测国际和国内旅行者传播病原体的方法。通过航空旅行,传染病在全球范围内迅速传播,而在机场实施监测系统有助于识别新出现的病毒并大规模追踪病原体。

papers.title_zh: 飞机废水病毒组监测揭示旅行者中的病毒多样性:一项来自印度古吉拉特邦的可行性研究。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Aircraft wastewater surveillance (AWS) at airports is an emerging method for detecting pathogens shed by international and domestic travellers. Global spread of infectious diseases occurs rapidly through air travel, and implementing surveillance systems at airports can help identify emerging viruses and track pathogens at scale. We aimed to characterize the viral diversity shed by travellers, which may represent routine viral circulation or active infection, at Ahmedabad airport in Gujarat. METHODS: We collected wastewater samples from domestic and international terminals where domestic flights connect to 18 states and 3 Union Territories, while international flights operate across 16 destinations in 11 countries. Samples were collected from June 2024 to November 2025. We used a capture probe-based enrichment approach for virome surveillance and detected multiple viruses of public health importance. RESULTS: We identified a total of 40 viral families and 315 viral species, with a median of 71 genomes/segments detected per sample in domestic wastewater and 48.5 genomes/segments per sample in international wastewater. We detected several respiratory and enteric viruses, including Influenza A virus, SARS-CoV-2, Human mastadenovirus A, Human mastadenovirus B, Noroviruses, Rotavirus A, Hepatitis A virus, Astrovirus MLB1, Human mastadenovirus F. Among these, certain viruses showed relatively higher mean RPKMF abundance in either domestic or international wastewater samples such as Bovine rotavirus A, Human rotavirus ID45/2, and BK polyomavirus observed in international wastewater samples, whereas Aichivirus A1, Norovirus GII.2, and Human immunodeficiency virus 1 showed higher abundance in domestic wastewater samples. We also detected multiple Influenza virus subtypes, including Influenza A subtypes H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, H7N1, and H9N2, along with Influenza B and Influenza C viruses. CONCLUSIONS: Continuous surveillance can provide early warning signals to public health authorities, timely decision-making and coordinated responses can reduce the spread of disease which also requires collaboration with national and international health authorities.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:机场的飞机废水监测(AWS)是一种新兴的检测国际和国内旅行者传播病原体的方法。通过航空旅行,传染病在全球范围内迅速传播,而在机场实施监测系统有助于识别新出现的病毒并大规模追踪病原体。我们旨在表征在古吉拉特邦艾哈迈达巴德机场传播的旅行者病毒多样性,这可能代表常规病毒循环或活跃感染。方法:我们从国内和国际航站楼采集废水样本,其中国内航班连接至18个州和3个联邦直辖区,而国际航班则运营至11个国家的16个目的地。样本采集时间为2024年6月至2025年11月。我们采用基于捕获探针的富集方法对病毒组监测进行分析,并检测了多种具有公共卫生重要性的病毒。结果:我们共鉴定出40个病毒家族和315种病毒,国内废水样本中每份检测到的基因组/片段中位数为71个,国际废水样本中为48.5个。我们检测到了多种呼吸道和肠道病毒,包括甲型流感病毒、SARS-CoV-2、人腺病毒A型、人腺病毒B型、诺如病毒、A型轮状病毒、甲型肝炎病毒、MLB1型星状病毒、人腺病毒F型。其中,某些病毒在国内外废水样本中表现出相对较高的平均RPKMF丰度,例如国际废水样本中检测到的牛轮状病毒A型、人轮状病毒ID45/2型和BK多瘤病毒,而A型甲型肝炎病毒、诺如病毒GII.2型和人类免疫缺陷病毒1型则在国内外废水样本中丰度较高。我们还检测到了多种流感病毒亚型,包括甲型流感病毒H1N1、H3N2、H5N1、H7N1和H9N2亚型,以及乙型和丙型流感病毒。结论:持续的监测可以为公共卫生部门提供早期预警信号,及时的决策和协调响应可以减少疾病的传播,这也需要与国家和国际卫生部门合作。

papers.title: Contact behavior and serological evidence of influenza reinfection across three post-COVID-19 pandemic seasons in a nationwide German cohort.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Influenza remains a global public health burden. While interpersonal contacts drive transmission, their association with individual-level reinfection risk is not well quantified, particularly in the post-COVID-19 period. We assessed the relationship between contact frequency and serological evidence of influenza reinfection across three consecutive seasons. METHODS: In this multicentre, population-based panel study conducted between 2020 and 2024, binding antibody titers against hemagglutinin antigens of three influenza subtypes (A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B) were measured by a bead-based multiplex immunoassay. Serological evidence of influenza reinfection was defined by fold-changes relative to the preceding season; with adjustments to minimize misclassification due to influenza vaccination. Logistic regression models were designed to estimate crude odds ratios (ORs) and DAG-informed adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for reinfection associated with total, household, and non-household contacts. RESULTS: Serological reinfection was detected in 14% (2021/22), 17% (2022/23), and 12% (2023/24) of participants. Among self-reported unvaccinated participants, reinfection was detected in 6%, 13% and 17% across the respective seasons. Non-household contacts were associated with increased odds of reinfection in one season (2022/23: aOR 1.008, 95% CI 1.002-1.014), while household contacts were associated with higher odds of reinfection in two seasons (2022/23: aOR 1.285, 95% CI 0.905-1.823; 2023/24: aOR 1.267, 95% CI 0.685-2.343). CONCLUSIONS: Serological evidence of reinfection among unvaccinated participants in comparison with all participants aligned more closely with surveillance data in 2021/22. Residual misclassification of vaccination or preceding infections may partly explain the absence of an association in 2021/22. Associations between contact behavior and reinfection were season-specific, with household contacts showing the strongest and most consistent effects.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Influenza remains a global public health burden. While interpersonal contacts drive transmission, their association with individual-level reinfection risk is not well quantified, particularly in the post-COVID-19 period.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This multicentre, population-based panel study was conducted between 2020 and 2024 in a nationwide German cohort. It included participants who were assessed for serological evidence of influenza reinfection across three consecutive seasons.
analysis.methods: Binding antibody titers against hemagglutinin antigens of three influenza subtypes (A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B) were measured by a bead-based multiplex immunoassay. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Associations between contact behavior and reinfection were season-specific, with household contacts showing the strongest and most consistent effects.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the role of contact behavior in influenza reinfection, which can inform targeted public health interventions and surveillance strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Residual misclassification of vaccination or preceding infections may partly explain the absence of an association in 2021/22. The evidence is moderate due to potential biases and limitations in serological classification.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the relationship between contact behavior and serological evidence of influenza reinfection in a nationwide German cohort across three post-COVID-19 pandemic seasons. The research aimed to quantify how interpersonal contacts influence individual reinfection risk. Using a bead-based multiplex immunoassay, antibody titers against influenza A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B subtypes were measured. The results showed varying reinfection rates across seasons, with household contacts consistently linked to higher odds of reinfection. The study highlights the season-specific nature of contact behavior's impact on reinfection and suggests potential biases in serological classification. These findings could inform public health strategies by emphasizing the importance of contact patterns in influenza transmission dynamics.

papers.title_zh: Contact behavior and serological evidence of influenza reinfection across three post-COVID-19 pandemic seasons in a nationwide German cohort.
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Influenza remains a global public health burden. While interpersonal contacts drive transmission, their association with individual-level reinfection risk is not well quantified, particularly in the post-COVID-19 period. We assessed the relationship between contact frequency and serological evidence of influenza reinfection across three consecutive seasons. METHODS: In this multicentre, population-based panel study conducted between 2020 and 2024, binding antibody titers against hemagglutinin antigens of three influenza subtypes (A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B) were measured by a bead-based multiplex immunoassay. Serological evidence of influenza reinfection was defined by fold-changes relative to the preceding season; with adjustments to minimize misclassification due to influenza vaccination. Logistic regression models were designed to estimate crude odds ratios (ORs) and DAG-informed adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for reinfection associated with total, household, and non-household contacts. RESULTS: Serological reinfection was detected in 14% (2021/22), 17% (2022/23), and 12% (2023/24) of participants. Among self-reported unvaccinated participants, reinfection was detected in 6%, 13% and 17% across the respective seasons. Non-household contacts were associated with increased odds of reinfection in one season (2022/23: aOR 1.008, 95% CI 1.002-1.014), while household contacts were associated with higher odds of reinfection in two seasons (2022/23: aOR 1.285, 95% CI 0.905-1.823; 2023/24: aOR 1.267, 95% CI 0.685-2.343). CONCLUSIONS: Serological evidence of reinfection among unvaccinated participants in comparison with all participants aligned more closely with surveillance data in 2021/22. Residual misclassification of vaccination or preceding infections may partly explain the absence of an association in 2021/22. Associations between contact behavior and reinfection were season-specific, with household contacts showing the strongest and most consistent effects.

papers.title: Study of Molecular Genetic Characteristics of Influenza A(H1N1) Viruses Identified During Monitoring in Kazakhstan (2023–2026)
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Seasonal influenza threatens global public health through rapid mutations. This study evaluated the prevalence and molecular-genetic characteristics of seasonal influenza viruses circulating in Kazakhstan during the 2023–2026 epidemic seasons. Methods: Nasopharyngeal swabs (n = 1756) and serum samples (n = 718) were screened using RT-qPCR, HI, and ELISA assays. Selected A(H1N1)pdm09 isolates underwent full-length HA and NA gene next-generation sequencing, followed by phylogenetic and phenotypic analyses. Results: Influenza A(H3N2) strains dominated in Kazakhstan during the 2023–2024 and 2025–2026 seasons. Conversely, the 2024–2025 season showed a shifting landscape, characterized by co-circulation of influenza B and A(H1N1)pdm09 strains belonging to genetic clade 6B.1A.5a.2a (subclades C.1.9 and C.1.9.3). Mutational mapping revealed ongoing in situ microevolution adjacent to the receptor-binding site (HA-R222K). Genomic screening of the NA gene identified critical I223R and S247N mutations traditionally linked to resistance. In silico profiling predicted that while the majority maintained baseline sensitivity, the solitary A/Shymkent/NRL-1999/2024 isolate harboring the I223R substitution exhibited a multidrug-resistant genotype to oseltamivir, peramivir, and zanamivir. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate dynamic inter-seasonal etiological shifts and the predicted emergence of an independent resistant lineage (NA-I223R). This underscores the necessity for continuous, expanded genomic surveillance of respiratory pathogens across Kazakhstan.

papers.title: Comparative immunogenicity and relative vaccine efficacy of recombinant and cell culture-based influenza vaccines: Results from a randomized trial of adults in the United States, 2024-2025
papers.abstract: Background: Recombinant (RIV) and cell culture-based inactivated (ccIIV) influenza vaccines could improve seasonal influenza prevention; however, evidence is limited in how protection may differ among non-egg-based vaccines. Methods: We conducted a randomized trial of RIV versus ccIIV to compare vaccine immunogenicity in adults aged 18 to 64 years during the 2024-25 influenza season (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06518577 ). Active surveillance for influenza-like illness was conducted for six months post-vaccination and cumulative incidence of influenza by vaccine type was compared to estimate relative vaccine efficacy. Participants were tested for influenza by reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction or rapid antigen tests. Immunogenicity was evaluated by hemagglutination inhibition (HAI), virus microneutralization (MN), and neuraminidase inhibition (NAI) assays in a subset of blood specimens collected pre-vaccination and one-month post-vaccination. Results: Among the 591 participants, 25 cases of influenza A were detected; 2.4% cumulative incidence among RIV recipients versus 6.1% among ccIIV recipients. The probability of influenza was 61% lower with RIV than ccIIV (95% confidence interval: 7 to 84). Among 151 participants, post-vaccination HAI and MN titers vaccine components were higher among RIV recipients while NAI titers were higher among ccIIV recipients. Conclusions: RIV provided better protection than ccIIV against influenza A illness in adults during the U.S.

Methods: We conducted a randomized trial of RIV versus ccIIV to compare vaccine immunogenicity in adults aged 18 to 64 years during the 2024-25 influenza season (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06518577 ). Active surveillance for influenza-like illness was conducted for six months post-vaccination and cumulative incidence of influenza by vaccine type was compared to estimate relative vaccine efficacy. Participants were tested for influenza by reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction or rapid antigen tests. Immunogenicity was evaluated by hemagglutination inhibition (HAI), virus microneutralization (MN), and neuraminidase inhibition (NAI) assays in a subset of blood specimens collected pre-vaccination and one-month post-vaccination. Results: Among the 591 participants, 25 cases of influenza A were detected; 2.4% cumulative incidence among RIV recipients versus 6.1% among ccIIV recipients. The probability of influenza was 61% lower with RIV than ccIIV (95% confidence interval: 7 to 84). Among 151 participants, post-vaccination HAI and MN titers vaccine components were higher among RIV recipients while NAI titers were higher among ccIIV recipients. Conclusions: RIV provided better protection than ccIIV against influenza A illness in adults during the U.S.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:重组(RIV)和基于细胞培养的灭活(ccIIV)流感疫苗可能改善流感预防;然而,关于非蛋基流感疫苗保护效果差异的证据有限。方法:我们进行了一项随机对照试验,比较RIV与ccIIV在2024-25流感季节18至64岁成人中的免疫原性(ClinicalTrials.gov,NCT06518577)。在接种疫苗后六个月,对流感样疾病的主动监测,并比较不同流感病毒类型引起的流感累积发病率,以估计相对疫苗效力。参与者通过逆转录聚合酶链反应或快速抗原检测进行流感诊断。免疫原性通过血凝抑制(HAI)、病毒微中和(MN)和神经氨酸酶抑制(NAI)试验在部分接种前和接种后一个月采集的血液样本中进行评估。结果:在591名参与者中,检测到25例流感A型病例;RIV接种者的累积发病率为2.4%,而ccIIV接种者为6.1%。RIV相较于ccIIV降低流感发生概率61%(95%置信区间:7至84)。在151名参与者中,接种后RIV接种者的血凝抑制和中和抗体滴度高于ccIIV接种者,而神经氨酸酶抑制滴度则更高。结论:在2024-25流感季节,RIV在成人中对流感A型疾病的保护效果优于ccIIV。

papers.title: Recurring Temporal Association Between Influenza A Epidemics and Subsequent Influenza B Dominance in Post-Pandemic Korea, 2022-2026.
papers.abstract: Post-pandemic influenza dynamics have shown unusual patterns globally. We investigated the re-emergence and recurrent seasonal dominance of influenza B in Korea across three post-pandemic seasons (2022-2026). We analyzed 157 consecutive weeks of national sentinel surveillance data (K-SenS, Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency), covering September 2022 to August 2025, plus preliminary data through Week 10 of 2026. Influenza B predominance was defined as weeks with > 50% influenza B among total influenza detections; a sensitivity analysis required overall influenza activity > 5%. Influenza B activity remained minimal during the 2022-23 season (mean proportion 3.3%; peak 25.3%) and never reached predominance. Two complete predominance episodes followed influenza A epidemics: after the 2023-24 epidemic (co-circulating A/H1N1pdm09 and A/H3N2; peak ILI 61.3/1000), B predominance began January 2024 and persisted 23 weeks (peak 100%); after the 2024-25A/H1N1pdm09-dominant epidemic (peak ILI 99.8/1000), it began February 2025 and accumulated 20 weeks over two periods with a brief interruption (peak 100%). Onset occurred 5-8 weeks after the influenza A peak by ILI (6-8 weeks virologically) in all three episodes, unaffected by threshold choice. A third episode following the 2025-26A/H3N2 epidemic was ongoing as of March 2026 (onset 7 weeks after the A peak). In post-pandemic Korea, influenza B repeatedly established seasonal dominance 5-8 weeks after influenza A epidemics across three consecutive seasons. This recurring temporal pattern may have implications for influenza surveillance, clinical preparedness, and vaccine strategy, though its underlying mechanism remains unestablished.

analysis.methods: The study used national sentinel surveillance data to analyze influenza activity, defining influenza B predominance as weeks with > 50% influenza B among total influenza detections. A sensitivity analysis required overall influenza activity > 5%.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the recurring temporal association between influenza A epidemics and subsequent influenza B dominance in post-pandemic Korea from 2022 to 2026. Using national sentinel surveillance data, it identifies two episodes of influenza B predominance following influenza A outbreaks, with each episode beginning 5-8 weeks after the A peak. The findings suggest a potential pattern that could influence influenza surveillance, clinical preparedness, and vaccine strategy, though the underlying mechanism remains unclear. The study's evidence is moderate due to its observational nature and lack of experimental validation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 后疫情时代流感的动态变化在全球范围内表现出异常模式。我们研究了韩国在三个后疫情时代季节(2022-2026)中流感B病毒的重新出现及其反复的季节性主导现象。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了157周连续的国家哨兵监测数据(K-SenS,韩国疾病控制与预防署),涵盖2022年9月至2025年8月,以及2026年第10周的初步数据。研究聚焦于韩国在三个后疫情时代季节中流感B病毒的主导情况。在2022-23季节,流感B活动水平保持较低,从未达到主导状态。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究利用国家哨兵监测数据分析流感活动,将流感B病毒活动占比超过50%的周定义为流感B主导。敏感性分析要求总体流感活动强度超过5%。
elements_zh.main_results: 在两次流感A流行之后出现了完整的流感B主导期:在2023-24季节(同时流行A/H1N1pdm09和A/H3N2;ILI峰值61.3/1000)之后,流感B主导始于2024年1月并持续了23周(峰值100%);在2024-25季节以A/H1N1pdm09为主导的流行(ILI峰值99.8/1000)之后,流感B主导始于2025年2月,并在两个时期累计持续了20周,中间有一次短暂中断(峰值100%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究观察到,在三个连续季节中,流感B病毒在流感A流行后5-8周反复建立季节性主导。这种反复的时间模式可能对流感监测、临床准备以及疫苗策略产生影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为后疫情时代韩国的流感监测策略、临床准备和疫苗规划提供信息,强调了监测流感A和B主导之间时间关系的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于监测数据,未能确定所观察模式的潜在机制。由于依赖观察性数据而非实验验证,证据强度中等。

This recurring temporal pattern may have implications for influenza surveillance, clinical preparedness, and vaccine strategy.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform influenza surveillance strategies, clinical preparedness, and vaccine planning in post-pandemic Korea, highlighting the need for monitoring the temporal relationship between influenza A and B dominance.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on surveillance data and does not establish the underlying mechanism of the observed pattern. The evidence is moderate due to the reliance on observational data without experimental validation.

papers.title_zh: 2022-2026年韩国流感A流行后流感B季节性主导的反复时间关联性
papers.source_body_en: Post-pandemic influenza dynamics have shown unusual patterns globally. We investigated the re-emergence and recurrent seasonal dominance of influenza B in Korea across three post-pandemic seasons (2022-2026). We analyzed 157 consecutive weeks of national sentinel surveillance data (K-SenS, Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency), covering September 2022 to August 2025, plus preliminary data through Week 10 of 2026. Influenza B predominance was defined as weeks with > 50% influenza B among total influenza detections; a sensitivity analysis required overall influenza activity > 5%. Influenza B activity remained minimal during the 2022-23 season (mean proportion 3.3%; peak 25.3%) and never reached predominance. Two complete predominance episodes followed influenza A epidemics: after the 2023-24 epidemic (co-circulating A/H1N1pdm09 and A/H3N2; peak ILI 61.3/1000), B predominance began January 2024 and persisted 23 weeks (peak 100%); after the 2024-25A/H1N1pdm09-dominant epidemic (peak ILI 99.8/1000), it began February 2025 and accumulated 20 weeks over two periods with a brief interruption (peak 100%). Onset occurred 5-8 weeks after the influenza A peak by ILI (6-8 weeks virologically) in all three episodes, unaffected by threshold choice. A third episode following the 2025-26A/H3N2 epidemic was ongoing as of March 2026 (onset 7 weeks after the A peak). In post-pandemic Korea, influenza B repeatedly established seasonal dominance 5-8 weeks after influenza A epidemics across three consecutive seasons. This recurring temporal pattern may have implications for influenza surveillance, clinical preparedness, and vaccine strategy, though its underlying mechanism remains unestablished.
papers.abstract_zh: 后疫情时代流感的动态变化在全球范围内表现出异常模式。我们研究了韩国在三个后疫情时代季节(2022-2026)中流感B病毒的重新出现及其反复的季节性主导现象。我们分析了157周连续的国家哨兵监测数据(K-SenS,韩国疾病控制与预防署),涵盖2022年9月至2025年8月,以及2026年第10周的初步数据。将流感B病毒活动占比超过50%的周视为流感B主导;敏感性分析要求总体流感活动强度超过5%。在2022-23季节,流感B活动水平保持较低(平均占比3.3%;峰值25.3%),从未达到主导状态。在两次流感A流行之后出现了完整的流感B主导期:在2023-24季节(同时流行A/H1N1pdm09和A/H3N2;ILI峰值61.3/1000)之后,流感B主导始于2024年1月并持续了23周(峰值100%);在2024-25季节以A/H1N1pdm09为主导的流行(ILI峰值99.8/1000)之后,流感B主导始于2025年2月,并在两个时期累计持续了20周,中间有一次短暂中断(峰值100%)。在所有三个案例中,流感B主导的开始时间均在流感A峰值后5-8周(病毒学上为6-8周),且不受阈值选择的影响。在2025-26季节以A/H3N2为主导的流行之后,流感B主导现象仍在持续(截至2026年3月),其开始时间为流感A峰值后7周。在后疫情时代的韩国,流感B病毒在三个连续季节中反复在流感A流行后5-8周建立季节性主导。这种反复的时间模式可能对流感监测、临床准备以及疫苗策略产生影响,尽管其潜在机制尚未明确。

papers.title: Structural characterization and antiviral activity of polysaccharide from Codonopsis pilosula.
papers.abstract: Codonopsis polysaccharides exhibit diverse biological activities, but their antiviral effects against the H1N1 influenza A virus and how these activities change after sulfation modification remains unclear. In this study, crude Codonopsis polysaccharide (COP) was obtained via water extraction and alcohol precipitation, and COP-1 (2.1 × 103 Da, β-D-(2 → 1)-fructan) was isolated and purified. Both COP and COP-1 were modified by sulfation using the sulfur trioxide-pyridine method, yielding derivatives SCOP and SCOP-1 with degrees of substitution of 1.792 and 1.403, respectively. Antiviral activity was evaluated in MDCK cells using MTT and TCID50 assays, revealing that COP, SCOP, and SCOP-1 all inhibited H1N1 replication, with sulfation significantly enhancing antiviral activity. Time-of-addition experiments indicated that inhibition occurred during the early phase of infection (0-4 h). Annexin V-PI staining confirmed that these compounds reduced virus-induced early apoptosis. In H1N1-infected A549 cells, they suppressed NF-κB p65 phosphorylation and downregulated the expression of IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1, CCL-5, TNF-α, and TRAIL. Overall, Codonopsis polysaccharides and their sulfated derivatives exert anti-influenza effects through a triple mechanism involving inhibition of early viral replication, anti-apoptotic activity, and anti-inflammatory action, making them promising candidates for antiflu therapeutics.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the antiviral effects of Codonopsis polysaccharides and their sulfated derivatives against the H1N1 influenza A virus. The research aimed to clarify the biological activities of these compounds and how sulfation modifies their antiviral potential. The study involved isolating and purifying crude polysaccharides, modifying them through sulfation, and evaluating their antiviral activity in MDCK cells. Results showed that all tested compounds inhibited H1N1 replication, with sulfation significantly enhancing this effect. Time-of-addition experiments suggested that inhibition occurs during the early phase of infection, and annexin V-PI staining confirmed reduced virus-induced apoptosis. Additionally, the compounds suppressed NF-κB p65 phosphorylation and downregulated inflammatory markers in infected A549 cells. These findings suggest that Codonopsis polysaccharides and their derivatives may offer a promising therapeutic approach for influenza treatment. However, the study is limited to in vitro experiments, and further research is needed to validate these results in vivo and in clinical settings.

papers.abstract_zh: 党参多糖表现出多种生物活性,但其对甲型H1N1流感病毒的抗病毒药物作用及其在硫酸化修饰后活性的变化仍不清楚。本研究通过水提醇沉法获得粗党参多糖(COP),并分离纯化出COP-1(2.1 × 103 Da,β-D-(2 → 1)-果聚糖)。采用三氧化硫-吡啶法对COP和COP-1进行硫酸化修饰,得到取代度分别为1.792和1.403的衍生物SCOP和SCOP-1。通过MTT和TCID50实验在MDCK细胞中评估抗病毒药物活性,结果显示COP、SCOP和SCOP-1均抑制了H1N1病毒的复制,硫酸化显著增强了抗病毒药物活性。时间添加实验表明,抑制作用发生在感染早期阶段(0-4小时)。通过Annexin V-PI染色确认这些化合物可减少病毒诱导的早期细胞凋亡。在H1N1感染的A549细胞中,它们抑制了NF-κB p65的磷酸化,并下调了IL-6、IL-8、MCP-1、CCL-5、TNF-α和TRAIL的表达。总体而言,党参多糖及其硫酸化衍生物通过抑制早期病毒复制、抗凋亡作用和抗炎作用三种机制发挥抗流感效果,显示出作为抗流感药物的潜力。

papers.title: Shifts in acute respiratory pathogen epidemiology: an 8-year surveillance study in Hangzhou, China (2018–2025)
papers.abstract: Objectives To analyze the epidemiological characteristics of six common respiratory pathogens in cases of Acute Respiratory Tract Infection (ARTI) in Hangzhou from 2018 to 2025, to provide a basis for clinical diagnosis and treatment, as well as public health prevention and control. Methods A multicenter retrospective study was conducted. Data from 81,974 ARTI cases from seven medical institutions in Hangzhou City between January 2018 and December 2025 were collected. Cases with positive test results were analyzed for influenza A virus (FluA), influenza B virus (FluB), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), adenovirus (ADV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP), and Chlamydia pneumoniae (CP), and statistical analysis was performed according to the pandemic stage, age, sex, season, and co-infection status. Results Among 81,974 patients, a total of 33,350 cases tested positive for pathogens, with an overall positive rate of 40.68%. MP (19.56%) and FluA (16.93%) were the most prevalent pathogens. The positivity rates of each pathogen showed statistically significant differences across the three stages before, during, and after the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic (all P < 0.001). Compared with the pre-COVID-19 pandemic period (2018–2019), the positive rates of FluA, FluB, and MP were significantly suppressed during the COVID-19 pandemic period (2020–2022), and then experienced a sharp “revenge rebound” in the post-COVID-19 pandemic period (2023–2025) (for example, the positive rate of MP rebounded from 5.43% to 21.09%). In contrast, the positive rates of RSV, ADV, and CP showed a persistent state of inhibition, but the absolute number of cases far exceeded that of before the COVID-19 pandemic. MP had the highest infection rate among 6– < 12 years old (38.31%), whereas FluA was more common in adults. The epidemiological distribution showed obvious seasonal heterogeneity: FluA/FluB/RSV were more prevalent in winter, MP was active in autumn, and ADV was more prevalent in summer. The co-infection rate was 7.22% (5,922 cases), and the most common combination was FluA + MP, accounting for 53.82% of all co-infections. Conclusion From 2018 to 2025, the pathogen spectrum of ARTI in Hangzhou was mainly composed of MP and FluA. The COVID-19 pandemic and related non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) have had a profound and heterogeneous impact on the epidemic pattern of respiratory pathogens. FluA, FluB, and MP showed the characteristics of “suppression-retaliatory rebound.” In the post-COVID-19 pandemic era, the activity of pathogens has clear seasonal, age, and gender distribution patterns, and the rate of mixed infections is high. The research results suggest that a dynamic monitoring system needs to be established, and targeted prevention and control measures should be implemented for key individuals and pathogens during high-incidence seasons.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在分析2018年至2025年间杭州急性呼吸道感染(ARTI)病例中六种常见呼吸道病原体的流行病学特征,为临床诊断和治疗以及公共卫生预防和控制提供依据。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用多中心回顾性研究设计,使用了2018年1月至2025年12月期间杭州七家医疗机构收集的81,974例急性呼吸道感染(ARTI)病例数据。
elements_zh.methods: 收集了2018年1月至2025年12月期间杭州七家医疗机构报告的81,974例急性呼吸道感染(ARTI)病例数据。对流感A病毒(FluA)、流感B病毒(FluB)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、腺病毒(ADV)、肺炎支原体(MP)和肺炎衣原体(CP)的阳性病例进行分析,并根据疫情阶段、年龄、性别、季节和混合感染状态进行统计分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 在81,974名患者中,共有33,350例检测出病原体,总体阳性率为40.68%。每种病原体的阳性率在新冠疫情(Coronavirus Disease 2019,COVID-19)大流行前、期间和后三个阶段中均表现出统计学上的显著差异(所有P < 0.001)。与新冠疫情前(2018–2019年)相比,新冠疫情大流行期间(2020–2022年)流感A型(FluA)、流感B型(FluB)和支原体(MP)的阳性率显著下降,随后在新冠疫情后(2023–2025年)出现了急剧的"报复性反弹"(例如,支原体的阳性率从5.43%反弹至21.09%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,在疫情和疫情后时期,流感A病毒、流感B病毒和肺炎支原体表现出“抑制-报复性反弹”的特征,具有明显的季节性、年龄和性别分布模式,并且混合感染率较高。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,需要建立动态监测系统,并在高发季节对关键人群和病原体实施针对性的预防和控制措施。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究是一项回顾性分析,可能会引入偏倚并限制建立因果关系的能力。研究证据基于大规模数据集,结果通过统计分析支持,表明具有中等程度的可信度。

papers.source_body_en: Objectives To analyze the epidemiological characteristics of six common respiratory pathogens in cases of Acute Respiratory Tract Infection (ARTI) in Hangzhou from 2018 to 2025, to provide a basis for clinical diagnosis and treatment, as well as public health prevention and control. Methods A multicenter retrospective study was conducted. Data from 81,974 ARTI cases from seven medical institutions in Hangzhou City between January 2018 and December 2025 were collected. Cases with positive test results were analyzed for influenza A virus (FluA), influenza B virus (FluB), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), adenovirus (ADV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP), and Chlamydia pneumoniae (CP), and statistical analysis was performed according to the pandemic stage, age, sex, season, and co-infection status. Results Among 81,974 patients, a total of 33,350 cases tested positive for pathogens, with an overall positive rate of 40.68%. MP (19.56%) and FluA (16.93%) were the most prevalent pathogens. The positivity rates of each pathogen showed statistically significant differences across the three stages before, during, and after the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic (all P < 0.001). Compared with the pre-COVID-19 pandemic period (2018–2019), the positive rates of FluA, FluB, and MP were significantly suppressed during the COVID-19 pandemic period (2020–2022), and then experienced a sharp “revenge rebound” in the post-COVID-19 pandemic period (2023–2025) (for example, the positive rate of MP rebounded from 5.43% to 21.09%). In contrast, the positive rates of RSV, ADV, and CP showed a persistent state of inhibition, but the absolute number of cases far exceeded that of before the COVID-19 pandemic. MP had the highest infection rate among 6– < 12 years old (38.31%), whereas FluA was more common in adults. The epidemiological distribution showed obvious seasonal heterogeneity: FluA/FluB/RSV were more prevalent in winter, MP was active in autumn, and ADV was more prevalent in summer. The co-infection rate was 7.22% (5,922 cases), and the most common combination was FluA + MP, accounting for 53.82% of all co-infections. Conclusion From 2018 to 2025, the pathogen spectrum of ARTI in Hangzhou was mainly composed of MP and FluA. The COVID-19 pandemic and related non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) have had a profound and heterogeneous impact on the epidemic pattern of respiratory pathogens. FluA, FluB, and MP showed the characteristics of “suppression-retaliatory rebound.” In the post-COVID-19 pandemic era, the activity of pathogens has clear seasonal, age, and gender distribution patterns, and the rate of mixed infections is high. The research results suggest that a dynamic monitoring system needs to be established, and targeted prevention and control measures should be implemented for key individuals and pathogens during high-incidence seasons.
papers.abstract_zh: 目的 分析2018年至2025年间杭州市急性呼吸道感染(ARTI)病例中六种常见呼吸道病原体的流行病学特征,为临床诊断和治疗以及公共卫生预防和控制提供依据。方法 开展了多中心回顾性研究。收集了2018年1月至2025年12月期间杭州市7家医疗机构的81,974例ARTI病例数据。对流感A病毒(FluA)、流感B病毒(FluB)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、腺病毒(ADV)、肺炎支原体(MP)和肺炎衣原体(CP)的阳性病例进行分析,并根据疫情阶段、年龄、性别、季节和混合感染状态进行统计分析。结果 在81,974例患者中,共检测出33,350例病原体阳性病例,总体阳性率为40.68%。MP(19.56%)和FluA(16.93%)是最常见的病原体。每种病原体的阳性率在新冠疫情(COVID-19)爆发前、爆发期间和爆发后三个阶段均表现出统计学显著差异(所有P < 0.001)。与新冠疫情爆发前(2018–2019年)相比,新冠疫情爆发期间(2020–2022年)FluA、FluB和MP的阳性率显著下降,而在新冠疫情爆发后(2023–2025年)则出现了明显的‘报复性反弹’(例如,MP的阳性率从5.43%反弹至21.09%)。相比之下,RSV、ADV和CP的阳性率表现出持续抑制状态,但病例的绝对数量远高于新冠疫情爆发前。MP在6–<12岁人群中感染率最高(38.31%),而FluA在成人中更为常见。流行病学分布显示出明显的季节性差异:FluA/FluB/RSV在冬季更为常见,MP在秋季活跃,ADV则在夏季更为普遍。混合感染率为7.22%(5,922例),最常见的组合是FluA + MP,占所有混合感染的53.82%。结论 2018年至2025年间,杭州市ARTI的主要病原体谱系由MP和FluA组成。新冠疫情及其相关的非药物干预措施(NPIs)对呼吸道病原体的流行模式产生了深远且异质性的影响。FluA、FluB和MP表现出‘抑制-报复性反弹’的特征。在新冠疫情后时期,病原体的活动呈现出明显的季节性、年龄和性别分布模式,混合感染率较高。研究结果表明,需要建立动态监测系统,并在高发病率季节对关键人群和病原体实施针对性的预防和控制措施。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在分析2018年至2025年间杭州急性呼吸道感染(ARTI)病例中六种常见呼吸道病原体的流行病学特征,为临床诊断和治疗以及公共卫生预防和控制提供依据。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用多中心回顾性研究设计,使用了2018年1月至2025年12月期间杭州七家医疗机构收集的81,974例急性呼吸道感染(ARTI)病例数据。
analysis_zh.methods: 收集了2018年1月至2025年12月期间杭州七家医疗机构报告的81,974例急性呼吸道感染(ARTI)病例数据。对流感A病毒(FluA)、流感B病毒(FluB)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、腺病毒(ADV)、肺炎支原体(MP)和肺炎衣原体(CP)的阳性病例进行分析,并根据疫情阶段、年龄、性别、季节和混合感染状态进行统计分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在81,974名患者中,共有33,350例检测出病原体,总体阳性率为40.68%。每种病原体的阳性率在新冠疫情(Coronavirus Disease 2019,COVID-19)大流行前、期间和后三个阶段中均表现出统计学上的显著差异(所有P < 0.001)。与新冠疫情前(2018–2019年)相比,新冠疫情大流行期间(2020–2022年)流感A型(FluA)、流感B型(FluB)和支原体(MP)的阳性率显著下降,随后在新冠疫情后(2023–2025年)出现了急剧的"报复性反弹"(例如,支原体的阳性率从5.43%反弹至21.09%)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,在疫情和疫情后时期,流感A病毒、流感B病毒和肺炎支原体表现出“抑制-报复性反弹”的特征,具有明显的季节性、年龄和性别分布模式,并且混合感染率较高。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,需要建立动态监测系统,并在高发季节对关键人群和病原体实施针对性的预防和控制措施。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究是一项回顾性分析,可能会引入偏倚并限制建立因果关系的能力。研究证据基于大规模数据集,结果通过统计分析支持,表明具有中等程度的可信度。

papers.title: Receptor-binding geometry constrains viral antigenic evolution through fitness-evasion coupling.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Although viral antigenic evolution is shaped by the competing demands of immune evasion and receptor-binding fitness, the physical principles underlying divergent viral evolutionary dynamics remain poorly understood. Here, by integrating structural biology, deep mutational scanning, and genomic surveillance data, we show that receptor-binding geometry constrains the spatial coupling between antibody escape and intrinsic viral fitness. In SARS-CoV-2, the exposed convex Spike-ACE2 interface spatially overlaps dominant neutralizing epitopes with receptor-contact residues, producing a stringent fitness-evasion trade-off. Consequently, viable escape mutations are largely restricted to a narrow peripheral region surrounding the receptor-binding core. As population immunity progressively saturates this limited escape space, continued adaptation increasingly requires coordinated saltational remodeling of the receptor-binding interface. In contrast, the influenza H3N2 hemagglutinin binds the small sialic acid ligand through a recessed pocket architecture that partially separates dominant antibody pressure from receptor-binding fitness constraints. This topological decoupling permits continuous stepwise antigenic drift without requiring frequent remodeling of the core binding site. Building on these findings, we develop a lightweight geometry-based framework that accurately identifies receptor-competitive antigenic hotspots across divergent viruses. Together, our results support a general model in which receptor geometry and protein surface topology strongly bias accessible antigenic evolutionary trajectories. IMPORTANCE: Why some viruses evolve through gradual antigenic drift whereas others undergo recurrent evolutionary leaps remains a fundamental question in virology. By integrating protein structures, mutational scanning data, and genomic surveillance, we show that the geometry of the receptor-binding interface strongly influences how immune escape mutations affect viral fitness. In SARS-CoV-2, receptor-binding residues are highly exposed and overlap with dominant antibody targets, restricting immune escape to a narrow set of mutations and promoting periodic evolutionary leaps when this space becomes exhausted. In contrast, the receptor-binding pocket of influenza A virus H3N2 is partially shielded from antibody recognition, allowing continuous antigenic drift with fewer fitness constraints. We further demonstrate that these structural principles can be used to identify antigenic hotspots directly from virus-receptor complexes. These findings provide a mechanistic explanation for divergent viral evolutionary trajectories and offer a structural framework for studying and anticipating antigenic evolution.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为预测和监测季节性流感病毒中的抗原性进化提供了机制基础,可以用于指导疫苗的开发和公共卫生策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅基于抽象层面的证据,结论基于来自多个来源的整合数据,支持中等置信度的评估。

papers.abstract_zh: 尽管病毒抗原性进化受到免疫逃逸和受体结合适应性的竞争需求的影响,但不同病毒进化动态背后的物理原理仍不明确。在这里,通过整合结构生物学、深度突变扫描和基因组监测数据,我们展示了受体结合几何结构如何限制抗体逃逸与内在病毒适应性之间的空间耦合。在SARS-CoV-2中,暴露的凸面刺突-ACE2界面与主要中和表位在空间上重叠,受体接触残基,从而产生严格的适应性逃逸权衡。因此,可行的逃逸突变主要局限于受体结合核心周围的狭窄外围区域。随着群体免疫逐渐填满这一有限的逃逸空间,持续适应越来越需要协调的受体结合界面突变重塑。相比之下,流感H3N2血凝素通过一个凹陷的口袋结构结合小的唾液酸配体,这种结构部分将主要抗体压力与受体结合适应性约束分离。这种拓扑解耦允许连续的逐步抗原漂移,而无需频繁重塑核心结合位点。基于这些发现,我们开发了一个轻量级的几何框架,能够准确识别不同病毒中的受体竞争性抗原热点。我们的结果共同支持了一个普遍模型,即受体几何结构和蛋白质表面拓扑结构强烈偏导可访问的抗原进化轨迹。重要性:为什么一些病毒通过渐进的抗原漂移进化,而另一些病毒则经历反复的进化跃迁,仍然是病毒学中的一个基本问题。通过整合蛋白质结构、突变扫描数据和基因组监测,我们展示了受体结合界面的几何结构如何影响免疫逃逸突变对病毒适应性的影响。在SARS-CoV-2中,受体结合残基高度暴露,并与主要抗体靶点重叠,限制了免疫逃逸突变的范围,并在该空间耗尽时促进周期性的进化跃迁。相比之下,流感A病毒H3N2的受体结合口袋部分被抗体识别所屏蔽,允许较少适应性约束下的连续抗原漂移。我们进一步证明,这些结构原理可用于直接从病毒-受体复合物中识别抗原热点。这些发现为病毒不同的进化轨迹提供了机制性解释,并为研究和预测抗原性进化提供了结构框架。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,受体几何结构和蛋白质表面拓扑结构强烈影响病毒可访问的进化轨迹,为理解抗原性进化提供了一个新颖的结构框架。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为预测和监测季节性流感病毒中的抗原性进化提供了机制基础,可以用于指导疫苗的开发和公共卫生策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅基于抽象层面的证据,结论基于来自多个来源的整合数据,支持中等置信度的评估。

papers.title: Disseminated BCG disease and recurrent pulmonary infections in a child with trisomy 21 carrying a novel BACH2 variant of uncertain significance: a 5-year case report
papers.abstract: Background Trisomy 21 is associated with combined immune dysregulation, including lymphopenia, impaired responses to vaccines, and heightened susceptibility to respiratory infections, driven in part by triplication of chromosome 21-encoded interferon receptor genes. BACH2 haploinsufficiency is a rare monogenic immunodeficiency characterized by lymphopenia, hypogammaglobulinemia, and susceptibility to infections and autoimmune diseases. Co-occurrence of these two conditions has not been previously described. Case presentation We report a 5-year longitudinal course in a Kenyan girl with trisomy 21, congenital heart disease, aspiration, and severe gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) found via whole exome sequencing to carry a heterozygous BACH2 missense variant (c.1420C > G;p.Leu474Val) of uncertain significance; parental segregation remains incomplete. In silico protein structural modeling (FoldX and Missense3D) yielded discordant predictions of the variant's effect on the protein’s stability and structure. Additional in silico pathogenicity predictions were also inconsistent: Sorting Intolerant from Tolerant (SIFT), Evolutionary Model of Variant Effect (EVE), PolyPhen-2, and CADD Phred scores predicted pathogenicity, while REVEL and AlphaMissense suggested a lack of deleteriousness. Persistent panlymphopenia and profoundly low IgM levels were documented throughout the follow-up period. Over these 5 years, the girl sustained six hospitalized lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs), with four requiring intensive care, which were disseminated Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) disease, respiratory syncytial virus and SARS-CoV-2 infections, and influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 pneumonia. Chest computed tomography at 4 years showed bilateral consolidations without bronchiectasis. Annual autoimmune screening remained negative. Conclusion This case illustrates the burden caused by severe and diverse respiratory pathogenic infections in a child with trisomy 21 and a candidate BACH2 variant. Trisomy 21 alone plausibly explains much of the phenotype; an independent contribution from the BACH2 variant remains unproven pending functional and segregation studies. Clinical considerations supported by this case include the potential value of prevaccination immunological screening to prevent BCG disease, equitable access to viral prophylaxis, and early specialist engagement in refractory cases.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Trisomy 21 is associated with combined immune dysregulation, including lymphopenia, impaired responses to vaccines, and heightened susceptibility to respiratory infections, driven in part by triplication of chromosome 21-encoded interferon receptor genes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A 5-year case report describes a Kenyan girl with trisomy 21, congenital heart disease, aspiration, and severe gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) who was found via whole exome sequencing to carry a heterozygous BACH2 missense variant (c.1420C > G;p.Leu474Val) of uncertain significance; parental segregation remains incomplete.
analysis.methods: The study involved longitudinal clinical observation, whole exome sequencing, and in silico protein structural modeling (FoldX and Missense3D) to assess the variant's effect on the protein’s stability and structure.
analysis.main_results: The girl sustained six hospitalized lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) over 5 years, with four requiring intensive care, including disseminated BCG disease, respiratory syncytial virus and SARS-CoV-2 infections, and influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 pneumonia. Chest computed tomography at 4 years showed bilateral consolidations without bronchiectasis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The case illustrates the burden caused by severe and diverse respiratory pathogenic infections in a child with trisomy 21 and a candidate BACH2 variant. The co-occurrence of these two conditions has not been previously described.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the potential value of prevaccination immunological screening to prevent BCG disease, equitable access to viral prophylaxis, and early specialist engagement in refractory cases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the lack of functional and segregation studies to confirm an independent contribution from the BACH2 variant, and the findings are based on a single case report.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 5-year longitudinal study of a Kenyan girl with trisomy 21 and a novel BACH2 variant, who experienced severe respiratory infections, including influenza A(H1N1)pdm09. The study highlights the immune dysregulation associated with trisomy 21 and the potential impact of a BACH2 variant. The findings suggest the importance of prevaccination immunological screening and early specialist involvement in managing refractory infections. However, the evidence is limited by the absence of functional studies to confirm the variant's role. The case adds to the understanding of immune-related complications in trisomy 21 and underscores the need for further research on BACH2 variants in this context.

papers.title_zh: 三体综合征21号染色体携带新型BACH2变异体的儿童出现播散性BCG疾病和反复肺部感染:一项5年随访病例报告
papers.source_body_en: Background Trisomy 21 is associated with combined immune dysregulation, including lymphopenia, impaired responses to vaccines, and heightened susceptibility to respiratory infections, driven in part by triplication of chromosome 21-encoded interferon receptor genes. BACH2 haploinsufficiency is a rare monogenic immunodeficiency characterized by lymphopenia, hypogammaglobulinemia, and susceptibility to infections and autoimmune diseases. Co-occurrence of these two conditions has not been previously described. Case presentation We report a 5-year longitudinal course in a Kenyan girl with trisomy 21, congenital heart disease, aspiration, and severe gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) found via whole exome sequencing to carry a heterozygous BACH2 missense variant (c.1420C > G;p.Leu474Val) of uncertain significance; parental segregation remains incomplete. In silico protein structural modeling (FoldX and Missense3D) yielded discordant predictions of the variant's effect on the protein’s stability and structure. Additional in silico pathogenicity predictions were also inconsistent: Sorting Intolerant from Tolerant (SIFT), Evolutionary Model of Variant Effect (EVE), PolyPhen-2, and CADD Phred scores predicted pathogenicity, while REVEL and AlphaMissense suggested a lack of deleteriousness. Persistent panlymphopenia and profoundly low IgM levels were documented throughout the follow-up period. Over these 5 years, the girl sustained six hospitalized lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs), with four requiring intensive care, which were disseminated Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) disease, respiratory syncytial virus and SARS-CoV-2 infections, and influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 pneumonia. Chest computed tomography at 4 years showed bilateral consolidations without bronchiectasis. Annual autoimmune screening remained negative. Conclusion This case illustrates the burden caused by severe and diverse respiratory pathogenic infections in a child with trisomy 21 and a candidate BACH2 variant. Trisomy 21 alone plausibly explains much of the phenotype; an independent contribution from the BACH2 variant remains unproven pending functional and segregation studies. Clinical considerations supported by this case include the potential value of prevaccination immunological screening to prevent BCG disease, equitable access to viral prophylaxis, and early specialist engagement in refractory cases.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:三体综合征21号染色体与联合免疫失调有关,包括淋巴细胞减少、对疫苗的反应受损以及对呼吸道感染的易感性增加,这在一定程度上是由21号染色体编码的干扰素受体基因三倍体引起的。BACH2单倍体不足是一种罕见的单基因免疫缺陷,表现为淋巴细胞减少、低丙种球蛋白血症以及对感染和自身免疫性疾病的易感性。这两种情况的共存尚未被描述过。病例报告:我们报告了一名肯尼亚女孩5年的随访过程,她患有三体综合征21号染色体、先天性心脏病、误吸和严重的胃食管反流病(GERD),通过全外显子组测序发现其携带一个意义未明的BACH2杂合错义变异体(c.1420C > G;p.Leu474Val);父母的遗传分离尚未完全明确。体外蛋白质结构建模(FoldX和Missense3D)对变异体对蛋白质稳定性和结构的影响预测不一致。其他体外病理性预测也存在不一致:Sorting Intolerant from Tolerant(SIFT)、Evolutionary Model of Variant Effect(EVE)、PolyPhen-2和CADD Phred评分预测该变异体具有致病性,而REVEL和AlphaMissense则认为其无致病性。在整个随访期间,均记录到持续的全淋巴细胞减少和显著降低的IgM水平。在5年期间,这名女孩经历了六次住院的下呼吸道感染(LRTIs),其中四次需要重症监护,包括播散性卡介苗(BCG)疾病、呼吸道合胞病毒和SARS-CoV-2感染,以及流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09肺炎。4岁时胸部计算机断层扫描显示双侧实变,但无支气管扩张。年度自身免疫筛查结果均为阴性。结论:该病例展示了三体综合征21号染色体和候选BACH2变异体的儿童所面临的严重且多样化的呼吸道病原体感染负担。三体综合征21号染色体本身可能解释了大部分表型;而BACH2变异体的独立贡献仍需功能研究和遗传分离研究来证实。本病例支持的临床考虑包括在预防BCG疾病前进行免疫学筛查的潜在价值、病毒预防药物的公平获取以及在难治性病例中早期专科介入的重要性。

papers.full_text: Article summary AI generated Seasonal influenza outbreaks exhibit significant variability in magnitude and timing across different regions, highlighting the need to understand the environmental factors influencing these patterns. This study found that rapid thermal transitions and deviations from long-term temperature norms are associated with increased influenza incidence in multiple cities, suggesting that these dynamics may provide valuable insights for predicting epidemic activity beyond traditional absolute temperature measures. Abstract Background Seasonal influenza outbreaks show strong temporal regularity, but their magnitude and timing vary across years and locations. This study examined whether thermal transition dynamics, in addition to absolute temperature, are associated with influenza incidence across contrasting climatic settings. Methods We conducted a retrospective multi-city analysis of Beijing, Tokyo, New York, London, and Sydney. City-specific climatological baselines were constructed from daily temperature records for 1965–2025 and compared with daily influenza incidence data for 2020–2025. Analyses considered long-term thermal seasonality, short-term temperature–incidence co-variation, temperature anomalies, daily temperature change (ΔT), and exploratory snowfall indicators. Results Descriptive analyses showed that increases in reported influenza incidence frequently coincided with rapid warming, delayed cooling, and larger departures from city-specific temperature baselines. In adjusted time-series analyses, ΔT remained associated with influenza incidence in several cities after accounting for seasonal structure and absolute temperature, although the direction and magnitude varied by city and lag period. Absolute temperature-anomaly magnitude showed less consistent independent associations, and the snowfall findings remained exploratory. Conclusions Thermal transition rate and deviation from long-term climatic norms may provide complementary information for describing the timing of influenza activity beyond absolute temperature alone. Because the analysis was observational and covered the COVID-19 pandemic period, the findings should be interpreted as temporal associations rather than causal effects. Further studies using longer influenza time series and additional environmental and surveillance covariates are needed. 1 Introduction Seasonal influenza exhibits a striking regularity across temperate regions, with recurrent outbreaks emerging during predictable periods of the year [1,2,3]. Despite this apparent seasonality, the magnitude, timing, and growth rate of influenza epidemics vary substantially across years and locations, even within the same climatic zone. Understanding the environmental drivers underlying this variability remains a central challenge in climate–health research. Ambient temperature has long been recognized as an important factor influencing respiratory virus transmission [2, 4, 5]. Experimental and epidemiological studies have demonstrated that lower temperatures can enhance viral stability, prolong aerosol persistence, and modulate host immune responses. However, empirical findings linking absolute temperature levels to influenza incidence have been inconsistent across regions and time periods. In many settings, similar winter mean temperatures are associated with markedly different epidemic intensities, suggesting that static climatic indicators alone may be insufficient to explain observed patterns. Recent work has increasingly emphasized the role of climatic variability and extremes, rather than mean conditions, in shaping health outcomes [6,7,8,9,10,11]. Rapid temperature fluctuations have been associated with excess mortality, cardiovascular events, and respiratory morbidity, pointing to the importance of short-term environmental stressors.Within this broader context, it is therefore relevant to examine whether influenza seasonality is associated not only with absolute temperature levels, but also with how quickly and irregularly environmental conditions change during seasonal transitions. In temperate climates, two transitional periods are particularly salient: the gradual cooling from late summer into autumn, and the warming phase from winter into spring. These periods are characterized by pronounced temperature gradients, increased day-to-day variability, and shifts in surface energy balance. Such conditions may plausibly generate transient mismatches between viral environmental stability and host physiological adaptation, potentially amplifying susceptibility at the population level, although this remains to be empirically validated. Yet, the epidemiological relevance of these thermal transition dynamics has received limited systematic investigation [6,7,8,9,10,11]. Recent influenza modeling studies have also examined stochastic epidemic dynamics and cross-country transmission-control patterns, highlighting the importance of dynamic processes and setting-specific heterogeneity [12, 13, 16]. Another climatic feature that has received comparatively little attention in influenza research is snowfall. Beyond its association with low temperature, snowfall represents a distinct physical process involving latent heat exchange and surface energy redistribution. Its potential relationship with short-term epidemic dynamics therefore warrants exploratory examination. However, snowfall has rarely been examined explicitly as a modifying factor in temperature–influenza relationships. This study addresses these gaps by examining seasonal thermal transition dynamics alongside absolute temperature, including rates of warming and cooling, departures from long-term climatic norms, and the occurrence of snowfall events. We conduct a multi-city analysis across five global metropolitan areas—Beijing, Tokyo, New York, London, and Sydney—spanning different climate regimes and both hemispheres. Using more than six decades of daily temperature records, we establish city-specific climatological baselines that characterize typical annual thermal cycles. These baselines provide a reference against which recent epidemic-period conditions can be evaluated. We then examine daily influenza-related incidence data from 2020 to 2025, a period that includes both seasonal influenza activity and the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on within-city temporal associations rather than cross-national burden comparisons. By integrating long-term climate context with short-term epidemiological dynamics, this study aims to explore whether and to what extent rapid thermal transitions, delayed seasonal cooling, and temperature anomalies are associated with changes in epidemic activity, and whether snowfall events correspond to measurable changes in incidence trajectories. By examining influenza seasonality in relation to temperature transitions as well as static thermal conditions, this work explores a dynamic perspective on climate–epidemic interaction under increasing climatic variability. Such an approach may be increasingly relevant under conditions of growing climate variability, where traditional seasonal assumptions are progressively disrupted. 2 Methods 2.1 Study design and data sources This study employed a retrospective observational design integrating long-term climatological records with short-term epidemiological time series to examine within-city temporal associations between seasonal temperature dynamics and influenza incidence. The analytical objective was to characterize how thermal transition processes relate to epidemic dynamics, rather than to predict disease outcomes or estimate absolute disease burden. Five metropolitan areas—Beijing, Tokyo, New York, London, and Sydney—were selected to represent diverse climate regimes, geographic settings, and both hemispheres, while also providing sufficiently long and continuous meteorological and epidemiological records for the study period. Daily mean surface air temperature data spanning 1965–2025 were obtained from publicly available global meteorological datasets providing long-term, station-based observations. These data were used exclusively to characterize city-specific climatological patterns and were not aggregated across locations. Epidemiological incidence data from 2020 to 2025 were derived from harmonized public health surveillance sources and national reporting systems. Influenza cases constituted the epidemiological outcome analyzed in this study and were analyzed separately from COVID-19 cases. COVID-19 case counts were not included in the influenza incidence series. Given heterogeneity in surveillance intensity and reporting practices across regions and over time, analyses focused on relative temporal variation within each city rather than cross-city comparisons of absolute incidence levels. All meteorological and epidemiological data used in this study were obtained from publicly accessible, aggregate databases; no private or individual-level participant data were used. All analyses were conducted using transparent, reproducible statistical procedures implemented in Python-based scientific computing libraries. No machine learning or artificial intelligence models were employed. The overall analytical framework, comprising climatic baseline construction, seasonal dynamics assessment, and anomaly-based transition analysis, is summarized in Fig. 1. An overview of the selected study cities, their climate characteristics, and data coverage is provided in Table 1. The study period (2020–2025) coincides with the COVID-19 pandemic and associated non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs), which substantially altered influenza transmission, surveillance, and testing patterns. COVID-19 cases were not included in the influenza incidence series. Accordingly, associations observed during this period were interpreted within the pandemic-affected surveillance context rather than as influenza-specific causal effects of climatic exposure. 2.2 Long-term climatic baseline construction To establish a reference framework for typical seasonal thermal conditions, a long-term daily climatological baseline was constructed for each city using the full 1965–2025 temperature record. For each calendar day \(d\in \{1,\dots ,365\}\), the baseline temperature \(\overline{T}_{d}\) was defined as: where \({T}_{y,d}\) denotes the observed daily mean temperature on day \(d\) in year \(y\), and \({N}_{d}\) represents the number of years with available observations for that calendar day. This procedure yields a smooth, city-specific annual thermal profile representing expected seasonal conditions. The resulting climatological baseline serves as a reference against which short-term temperature deviations and anomalous thermal transitions during recent epidemic periods can be evaluated. The overall procedure for constructing city-specific long-term climatic baselines is summarized in Fig. 2. 2.3 Seasonal temperature transition metrics Short-term thermal transitions were quantified using the daily temperature change rate, defined as: where \({T}_{t}\) is the daily mean temperature on day \(t\). This metric captures the speed and direction of warming or cooling independently of absolute temperature level. To reduce high-frequency noise in epidemiological reporting, daily influenza incidence was smoothed using a centered 7-day moving average: nitial associations between temperature transition metrics and epidemic activity were assessed descriptively using Pearson correlation analysis, focusing on within-city temporal co-variation between thermal change rates and incidence patterns. Because both climatic and epidemiological variables exhibit strong seasonal structure, additional seasonality-adjusted time-series analyses were conducted as described in Section G (Fig. 3). 2.4 Temperature anomalies relative to climatological norms To assess departures from expected seasonal thermal conditions, daily temperature anomalies were calculated relative to the long-term climatological baseline. For each day \(t\), the temperature anomaly \({A}_{t}\) was defined as: where \(\overline{T}_{d\left( t \right)}\) denotes the baseline temperature corresponding to the calendar day of \(t\). Both signed anomalies and absolute anomaly magnitudes \(\mid {A}_{t}\mid \) were examined. The absolute anomaly was used as an indicator of the intensity of climatic deviation, independent of whether conditions were warmer or cooler than expected. Associations between temperature anomalies and influenza incidence were evaluated descriptively to examine whether unusual thermal conditions co-varied with epidemic activity. The derivation of temperature anomaly and thermal transition metrics and their linkage to incidence analysis are summarized in Fig. 4. Definitions of all climatic and epidemiological variables used in the analysis are summarized in Table 2. 2.5 Humidity as a complementary climatic variable To incorporate additional environmental context relevant to respiratory virus transmission, relative humidity (RH) was included as a complementary climatic variable in the analysis. Daily RH data for each city were obtained from the same meteorological data sources as temperature records and processed using identical temporal alignment procedures. To ensure consistency with temperature-based analyses, RH time series were smoothed using a centered 7-day moving average to reduce short-term variability associated with reporting noise. A long-term climatological baseline for RH was constructed using the full available historical record, analogous to the temperature baseline. Daily humidity anomalies were defined as deviations from the corresponding calendar-day climatological mean. Associations between RH, RH anomalies, and influenza incidence were assessed descriptively, focusing on within-city temporal co-variation rather than cross-city comparability. RH was included as a supporting environmental variable rather than as a primary explanatory variable or an estimate of an independent effect. 2.6 Snowfall as an environmental modifier Snowfall events were identified using binary indicators derived from meteorological records. Days with snowfall were marked as \({S}_{t}=1\), and all other days as \({S}_{t}=0\). Snowfall was examined as a modifying environmental indicator rather than as a primary explanatory variable. Rather than assuming a direct causal relationship, snowfall was treated as an exploratory environmental marker associated with seasonal progression, with particular attention to temporal changes in epidemic activity around snowfall events. 2.7 Statistical analysis and reproducibility To distinguish associations with thermal transitions from those attributable to shared seasonal patterns, adjusted time-series analyses were conducted separately for each city. Daily influenza case counts were modelled using Poisson log-linear regression with a log link. Model coefficients were estimated by maximum likelihood using iteratively reweighted least squares. The principal exposure variables were daily temperature change (ΔT) and absolute temperature-anomaly magnitude, which were evaluated in separate models at lags of 0, 7, 14, and 21 days. Lags were defined using exact calendar-day displacement rather than row displacement, thereby preventing observations separated by gaps in the seasonal surveillance records from being treated as consecutive days. Each model included the thermal exposure of interest, absolute daily temperature, two pairs of Fourier terms representing annual and semi-annual seasonal cycles, categorical influenza-season indicators, and day-of-week indicators. Temporal autocorrelation and heteroskedasticity were addressed using a heteroskedasticity- and autocorrelation-consistent sandwich covariance matrix with a Bartlett kernel and a maximum lag of 21 days. Autocovariance contributions were restricted to observations from the same influenza season and separated by the corresponding number of consecutive calendar days. Adjusted rate ratios (RRs) were obtained by exponentiating the exposure coefficients and are reported with autocorrelation-consistent 95% confidence intervals and two-sided p values. The Benjamini–Hochberg procedure was applied across the lag-specific analyses to control the false discovery rate, with q < 0.05 considered statistically significant. A structured summary of the analytical components, input datasets, and corresponding outputs is provided in Table 3. 3 Results 3.1 Long-term climatic baselines across cities Across all five cities, the 60-year mean daily temperature profiles exhibit smooth, unimodal seasonal cycles characteristic of their respective climate regimes (Fig. 5a–e). Northern Hemisphere cities (Beijing, London, Sydney, New York, and Tokyo) display synchronized seasonal timing, with temperature minima in winter and maxima in summer, while Sydney exhibits an approximately 6-month phase shift consistent with its Southern Hemisphere location. Despite substantial differences in absolute temperature ranges—ranging from the continental amplitude observed in Beijing to the more moderate maritime profile of London—the long-term baselines within each city remain stable and regular. These climatological baselines provide a consistent reference against which short-term thermal deviations and epidemic-period dynamics can be evaluated. 3.2 Seasonal temperature–incidence co-variation (2020–2025) Across all cities, influenza incidence during 2020–2025 exhibits pronounced seasonal structure when plotted alongside daily temperature (Fig. 6a–e). Visual comparison shows that increases in incidence frequently coincide with seasonal transition periods, including autumnal cooling and early spring warming, although these descriptive patterns do not by themselves distinguish thermal-transition associations from shared seasonality. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to understand how seasonal thermal transitions influence influenza incidence across multiple cities, addressing the challenge of identifying environmental drivers of variability in outbreak patterns.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a retrospective observational design integrating long-term climatological records with short-term epidemiological time series, focusing on Beijing, Tokyo, New York, London, and Sydney from 1965–2025. Influenza cases were analyzed separately from COVID-19 cases, with daily incidence smoothed using a 7-day moving average.
analysis.methods: Daily influenza incidence was smoothed using a centered 7-day moving average to reduce high-frequency noise. Associations between temperature transition metrics and epidemic activity were assessed descriptively using Pearson correlation analysis, focusing on within-city temporal co-variation. Relative humidity was included as a complementary climatic variable, also smoothed using a 7-day moving average, and analyzed for within-city temporal co-variation.
analysis.main_results: Descriptive analyses showed that increases in reported influenza incidence frequently coincided with rapid warming, delayed cooling, and larger departures from city-specific temperature baselines. Absolute temperature-anomaly magnitude showed less consistent independent associations, and the snowfall findings remained exploratory.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that thermal transition rate and deviation from long-term climatic norms may provide complementary information for describing the timing of influenza activity beyond absolute temperature alone.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that thermal transition dynamics could inform improved surveillance and prediction models for influenza activity, particularly in pandemic-affected contexts where traditional measures may be less reliable.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study focused on relative temporal variation within each city rather than cross-city comparisons, and analyses were conducted within the context of pandemic-affected surveillance, which may limit generalizability. The evidence is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the relationship between seasonal thermal transitions and influenza incidence across multiple cities, highlighting the variability in outbreak patterns and the need to understand environmental influences. Using a retrospective observational design, the researchers integrated long-term climatological data with short-term epidemiological time series, analyzing Beijing, Tokyo, New York, London, and Sydney. Daily influenza incidence was smoothed using a 7-day moving average, and associations with temperature transition metrics were assessed descriptively. Results indicated that rapid warming, delayed cooling, and deviations from city-specific temperature baselines were frequently linked to increased influenza reports. The authors suggested that thermal transition rates and deviations from climatic norms may offer additional insights into influenza timing beyond absolute temperature. However, the study focused on relative variation within cities and considered the impact of pandemic-related changes in surveillance, which may affect the generalizability of findings. The evidence is moderate, as the study did not employ machine learning or AI models and relied on descriptive analyses.
